days.quote: Every time you let someone mistreat you, you lose a piece of yourself. Don’t lose all of you to keep a little of them.
days.caption:
You don't have to lose yourself to keep someone.

Every time I let it slide, I gave away a little more of me.
I called it patience. It was just me getting smaller.
Some people are only worth keeping if you get to stay whole too.

Which part of you are you taking back this week?

days.quote: Don’t shrink yourself because someone can’t see your worth.
days.action: a big proud stretch, arms open wide
days.caption:
You were never too much. They were just looking from too far away.

I used to make myself smaller in rooms that didn't get me.
Quieter. Softer. Easier to ignore.
It never made them see me. It only made me forget myself.

Where do you still shrink without noticing?

days.quote: POV: you finally chose yourself and felt guilty about it. That guilt isn’t a sign you did wrong. It’s a sign you’re growing.
days.action: watering a sprout in a tiny clay pot until it blooms
days.caption:
Choosing yourself can feel wrong at first. It isn't.

The first time I said no without explaining, I felt sick about it for a whole day.
I kept waiting to be punished for it.
Nothing bad happened. I just got a little more room to grow.

What did you choose for yourself lately, even if it felt strange?

days.quote: Then: one text left on “seen.” Twenty theories. Zero sleep. Now: one text left on “seen.” “They’re probably busy.” Goodnight. Same text. Softer you.
The right people give you wings. The wrong ones give you lessons your soul never asked for. Choose truly.
Don’t teach your soul to settle for what suffocates it. Let it breathe.
Life isn’t a race. It’s a road, and you deserve to walk it at your own pace.
Your life is a blackboard. Make sure only you hold the chalk.
Their opinion isn’t your destiny. Rise, and let your work speak.
A tree stands only as long as its roots are strong. Your roots are your soul. Heal them first.
Some understand you in a moment. For others, a lifetime isn’t enough.
Everyone says: rest when you’re done. Done with the emails, the chores, everyone else’s needs. Nobody says: you’re never “done.” So rest before you’re empty.
Read this if everyone around you seems ahead. Promotions. Weddings. New cities. And you’re still figuring out Tuesday. You’re not behind. You were busy surviving.
I miss the version of me who… sang loudly in the car… ate cake for breakfast… laughed without checking who was watching. She’s not gone. She’s waiting for me to let her play again.
Healing isn’t one big moment. It’s a glass of water, an early night, one honest text, a walk without your phone… a hundred small, ordinary days.
